title: Serve the daemon: Node HTTP listener and runnable daemon entrypoint
description:
Objective: make the daemon a process that serves. Bind the committed pure HTTP boundary to a real socket and give apps/daemon an entrypoint, so an external consumer — browser, MCP host, canary, IDE adapter — can actually reach production authority. Created by governor-f70d1157 at human direction 2026-08-09 12:57Z. A governor created this task; an ARCHITECT must plan it. The description below is measurement and constraint, not a plan.

WHY THIS EXISTS. The pure boundary is FULLY BUILT and nothing serves it. This is global rail Clause 1 at the largest scale on the board: exporting symbols is not composition, and here not even the export happened.

MEASURED ON DISK by governor-f70d1157 at 12:56Z, and re-verified independently after a worker reported it:
- `grep -rE "createServer\(|\.listen\(|Deno\.serve|Bun\.serve" apps packages adapters --include=*.ts --include=*.js` (node_modules and tests excluded) returns ZERO. There is no HTTP listener anywhere in this repository.
- apps/daemon/package.json declares NO "main" and NO "bin". Its only scripts are typecheck and test. The daemon cannot be started; it is a library.
- No server/, transport/ or adapters/ directory exists anywhere.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so nothing here is rebuilt (verify each on disk before naming it):
- apps/daemon/src/http/http-adapter.ts:150 exports `handleCommandRequest` — the pure request handler. This is the thing to serve.
- apps/daemon/src/http/http-contract.ts holds the whole boundary vocabulary: HTTP_BOUNDARY_ERROR_CODES, HTTP_REFUSAL_STAGES, HTTP_INPUT_BOUNDS, MAX_COMMAND_PAYLOAD_FIELDS, WIRE_PROTOCOL_VERSION, AuthVerdict/AuthenticatedPrincipal/AuthenticationResult/Authenticator, CommandDecisionPort, CommandRegistry, CommandRegistryEntry, CommandAdapterDeps, HttpCommandRequest, HttpRefused.
- apps/daemon/src/http/event-stream.ts exports `readEventPage` and `resumeFromSnapshot`, and they ARE already on the daemon root (index.ts:101), along with EVENT_STREAM_LAYER, EVENT_STREAM_REFUSAL_CODES and MAX_EVENT_PAGE_SIZE.
- The command handler tables are all on the root: BOOTSTRAP_HANDLERS/runBootstrapCommand, GOAL_HANDLERS, PLANNING_HANDLERS, REVIEW_HANDLERS, claimWork/parseWorkRequest, evaluateDoctorCommandBytes.
- NEITHER http-adapter.ts NOR http-contract.ts is exported from apps/daemon/src/index.ts. Confirmed absent.

WHAT THIS TASK LANDS, three things and no more:
1. A Node HTTP listener (node:http; no third-party server dependency) that accepts a request, decodes it within the committed HTTP_INPUT_BOUNDS, and delegates to `handleCommandRequest`. The listener DECIDES NOTHING — it is transport only. Every refusal must be the boundary's own code, stage and refusing layer, surfaced unchanged; a status code mapped by the listener must not lose or translate them.
2. A daemon entrypoint so the process can be started, plus whatever package.json wiring makes it runnable. Fail closed on startup: a listener that cannot bind, or that is handed an incomplete CommandAdapterDeps, must refuse with a stable code and exit non-zero rather than serving a partial surface.
3. Root publication of the HTTP boundary from apps/daemon/src/index.ts, following the pattern task-6054520bc and task-f5d1dae629 already established for this file, so an external consumer can name the request/refusal types without a deep import.

NOT in scope, and this list is binding: changing ANY behaviour in http-adapter.ts, http-contract.ts, event-stream.ts or any handler; TLS/certificates; MCP stdio or streamable-HTTP transport; authentication POLICY (the Authenticator port is consumed, never implemented here); CORS beyond what a same-origin control room needs; process supervision, daemonisation or service installation; new commands or new authority of any kind.

WHO IS WAITING. Name these as consumers per Clause 1 rather than leaving the edge implied: task-3f503779 (Real-browser journey harness — blocked at planning on exactly this, by its own author), task-667b1085 (Control-room journey gate), task-05ce9b8f (Security fault matrix, which needs an HTTP/event-stream authority subject), and task-97554aa4 (Foundation self-host canary). This task does not certify any of their journeys; it makes them possible.

Hard dependencies: none. Every surface named above is committed at HEAD.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck, PLUS a real listening probe — start the process, issue a request over a real socket, assert the response, and shut it down cleanly. A test that calls handleCommandRequest in-process proves nothing this task is for.

Size: if the plan exceeds 12 steps or 10 distinct affectedFiles, SPLIT IT — the entrypoint and the root publication are separable from the listener. Say so rather than padding.
definitionOfDone: A Node HTTP listener exists, built on node:http with no third-party server dependency, that binds a real socket and delegates every accepted request to the committed handleCommandRequest from apps/daemon/src/http/http-adapter.ts. The listener contains no command dispatch, no authority decision, and no policy of its own.

The daemon is a runnable process: apps/daemon declares an entrypoint and can be started from a clean shell without a bundler step. Startup fails CLOSED — a socket that cannot bind, or incomplete CommandAdapterDeps, refuses with a stable reason code and a non-zero exit rather than serving a partial surface.

Refusals cross the transport unchanged. A test asserts, for at least one case per HTTP_REFUSAL_STAGES value, that the boundary's own error code, stage and refusing layer appear in the response and are not translated, collapsed, or replaced by a bare status code. Per epic rail 6 this asserts the specific code, never merely that the request failed.

Input bounds are enforced at the socket, not only in the pure layer: a request exceeding HTTP_INPUT_BOUNDS or MAX_COMMAND_PAYLOAD_FIELDS is refused with its exact code before any handler runs, and the test proves the handler was not reached rather than only that the response was a refusal.

apps/daemon/src/index.ts publishes the HTTP boundary — the request/refusal types and vocabularies a consumer needs to drive and discriminate — following the curated named-export pattern already in that file. index-surface.test.ts's EXPECTED_EXPORTS list and its cardinality guard are both updated with the new names; a bare count bump with no names added defeats the guard and is a rejection.

A REAL LISTENING PROBE is the completion evidence, recorded verbatim: start the process, issue a request over an actual socket to the bound port, assert the response body and status, and shut down cleanly with no leaked handle. An in-process call to handleCommandRequest does not satisfy this DoD — it is precisely what already exists and precisely what does not serve.

Zero behaviour change in the pure layer: git diff shows no edit to http-adapter.ts, http-contract.ts, event-stream.ts, or any handler module. pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck all exit 0, with foreign red attributed by path per global rail 3 and disclosed verbatim.
taskRails: The listener is TRANSPORT ONLY. It decodes, bounds-checks, delegates, and serialises. If you find yourself writing a condition that decides whether a command is allowed, who the caller is, or what a refusal means, stop — that authority already lives in http-adapter.ts and http-contract.ts and a second copy will drift from it.

Consume the Authenticator port; do not implement an authentication policy. http-contract.ts defines Authenticator, AuthVerdict, AuthenticatedPrincipal and AuthenticationResult. Wire them. Inventing a credential scheme here is out of scope and is a report_blocked, not a judgement call.

Read http-adapter.ts and http-contract.ts end to end before naming a single symbol; verify every name on disk rather than copying it from this description (skill: explore-before-assume). This description was written by a governor from greps, not by the module's author.
node:http only. No express, fastify, koa, or any third-party server package. No new runtime dependency in any package.json without reporting blocked first.

PROVE IT OVER A REAL SOCKET. A green vitest suite that calls handleCommandRequest in-process is exactly the evidence that already exists and exactly what this task is fixing. The completion probe must bind a port, connect to it, and shut down cleanly.
Keep each production source focused: target <=250 physical lines, split before 400. The listener, the entrypoint and the root publication are three concerns — do not let them become one file.
Never export a test-only module. http/event-stream-fixtures.ts and http/http-test-fixtures.ts stay internal; the index-surface set-equality list must keep denying them.

Commit by explicit pathspec only — never a bare git commit or git add -A. Several agents share this working directory and completion hooks have swept foreign files into four separate commits today. Hand QA blob shas (git hash-object <path>) alongside a base-ref diff, not a commit sha; if a foreign hook has already swept your files, do NOT amend it and do NOT create an empty commit.

Hand-author exactly one case for each member of `HTTP_REFUSAL_STAGES`, assert the generated count and stage-set equality, and pin status plus `AUTHENTICATION_FAILED/AUTHENTICATE`, `DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH/COMPATIBILITY`, `INPUT_INVALID/DECODE`, `INPUT_INVALID/REGISTRY`, `CAPABILITY_DENIED/AUTHORIZE`, `INPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED/PAYLOAD_SHAPE` with `COMMAND_PAYLOAD_FIELDS`, and the verbatim `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT/DISPATCH/DURABLE_DECISION` port refusal.
